To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) disentanglement is a property of the data generating process, and not the data, (ii) disentangement scores do not capture this, and (iii) disentangling latent correlations is a feasible task.

(1) most prominent disentanglement methods learn meaningful latent representations, but (2) widely used disentangled representation learning metrics do not capture the latent correlations that are present in the data, and (3) these latent correlations can be disentangled using weak supervision, if we constrain this to be causally plausibel.

(1) latent representations of state-of-the-art disentanglement methods reflect correlations in the data; (2) widely used disentangle ment scores do not capture these correlations; (3) weak supervision is sufficient to learn disentangled representations of correlated latent variables; and (4) our findings support the argument to model independent mechanisms rather than factors of variation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to learn meaningful representations from correlated data.
the question of whether and how disentangled representations can be learned from data with correlations, and what the implications for disentanglement evaluation are.

the question: "Can a disentangled representation be learned from data that is correlated?" We show that this can be achieved with a simple and efficient method, which is able to learn meaningful latent correlations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
disentangled representations are learned in correlated data, while existing disentanglement measures are unable to capture this disentanglement.
the current disentanglement methods are not able to capture the latent structure in the data, but that it is possible to learn this structure with additional supervision.
disentanglement is an important goal, but the existing methods and scores are not sufficient for this task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we analyze the behavior of disentanglemenet models and disentanglemenent scores on correlated data, and propose a method to disentangle latent correlations using weakly supervised information.
the disentanglement community should shift the focus from independent variables to independent mechanisms.
disentangled representations are not only learned from independent factors of variations but also from latent correlations in the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we should be cautious when evaluating and comparing disentanglement methods on synthetic datasets, and that we need to develop new disentanglement evaluation methods that are better suited to the real-world scenarios.
the disentanglement literature has so far largely ignored correlations in the data.
disentanglement methods can be applied to correlated data and that the learned representations are meaningful, but we also show how disentanglement can fail in such settings.
